title: 2003 AMC 12A Problem 9
statement: A set \(S\) of points in the \(xy\)-plane is symmetric about the origin, both coordinate axes, and the line \(y = x.\) If \((2, 3)\) is in \(S,\) what is the smallest number of points in \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Reflecting across \(y=x\) gives \((3,2),\) and reflecting across the axes gives all points \((\pm2,\pm3)\) and \((\pm3,\pm2).\)

There are \(8\) such points, and this set is already symmetric about the origin, both axes, and \(y=x.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The symmetries produce every sign choice and coordinate swap
